Issued at 336 AM CDT Wed Sep 9 2026

The mid-level ridge that has been in place across the central CONUS 
for what seemed like an eternity has effectively flattened. This in 
response to the former western portion of the Omega Block lifting NE 
into the Northern Plains and Canadian Plains and a trailing mid-
level shortwave rounding its base. The surface low reflection of the 
main mid-level feature has pushed a frontal boundary southward into 
the region, and has begun to push into/through northern Missouri and 
NE Kansas. Given the shallower nature of the boundary, shower and 
storm activity is displaced north of the surface front, tied more 
closely to the LLJ and 850mb front. While the low levels remain 
quite dry, stabilization in the lowest levels and lack of 
strong/robust storm cores should severely limit downbursts potential. 
The overnight environment really is more conducive to a flooding 
threat given the parallel shear/steering flow and moisture 
transport. Fortunately, a more scattered nature limits truly short-
duration rainfall and most areas should be able to handle 2.5 to 5 
inches of rainfall or more over 3 to 6 hr durations, via RFC FFG. 
Areas that saw storms the other day, mainly western Missouri into 
far eastern Kansas, may be on the lower end of that range. A slowing 
trend to the frontal passage also increases flood potential a tinge.

As just mentioned, recent CAM guidance has continued to slow the 
overall frontal progression, now potentially not to the east-west 
portions of the Missouri River until 18z. This will potentially 
cause a couple of main deviations from the initial forecast. First, 
it may yield a window of highs into the mid-upper 90s (yes, 
again...) for areas around the KC Metro southward. Northern portions 
of that may only see a couple/few hrs of this heat before the front 
and/or convection occurs, but southern areas may have a full day of 
this. Including heat index values pushing around 105 again. Thus, 
there will be a very small Heat Advisory for today. Right now, it 
will NOT include the KC Metro considering it may be quite short 
duration. The slower progression potentially pulls the strong/severe 
storm threat back northward a bit. While SB/MUCAPE depictions are 
not wholly different with muddled mid-level lapse rates in place, 
the difference becomes more clear when you view point soundings. 
Deep inverted-V soundings near/south of the front vs elevated nature 
north of. Primarily it would increase the damaging wind gust / 
downburst threat. Small hail would remain in play, but organized 
storms appear difficult to come by with better shear profiles north, 
but the thermodynamic profiles remain fairly poor. Initial storms 
would tend to carry the greatest risk before increasing areal 
coverage and training storms moisten the low levels. The SPC 
Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) remains fairly well placed, maybe a 
tinge south given recent trends, and is driven solely by wind. 

By Wednesday night/overnight this activity shifts further south and 
out of the immediate area. And with that... the prolonged heat 
officially over for the entirety of the CWA. Highs fall back closer 
to seasonal norms with forecast highs in the 80s tending to prevail 
through the weekend and into early next week. The next opportunity 
for precipitation moves through this weekend Friday night and again 
Saturday night as a couple of mid-level shortwaves move through the 
more zonal flow. Current deterministic depictions suggest the 
potential for a couple rounds of thunderstorm activity. Right now, 
highest confidence is just west into Kansas, but would drift into 
the area from NW to SE and then W/SW to E/NE respectively. Of casual 
note, depending on the evolution the next couple of cycles, this 
could also include the potential for flooding potential by Saturday 
night/overnight as current depictions show a developing surface low 
and the warm frontal position possibly across northern Kansas and 
into Missouri somewhere between Highway 36 and I-70 corridors. That 
would be on top of anything received Friday night. Plenty of time to 
evolve, but would be the next window to watch.
